proposed_fixes.title: Always On Top can lose taskbar coverage during Dota 2 push-to-talk
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A game or push-to-talk focus/window transition may change topmost/z-order state or taskbar auto-hide activation without triggering Always On Top refresh.
plan: Reproduce with Dota 2 borderless mode and track window z-order/taskbar activation before and after push-to-talk.
Restore the pinned window's topmost state only when the game transition removes it.
Add a targeted regression check for the push-to-talk transition.
verification: In a borderless Dota 2 solo game, use push-to-talk and move the pointer to the taskbar edge; verify the taskbar stays hidden behind the pinned window.

confidence.rationale: The game/OS focus transition may disturb z-order; the reported link to party/solo mode and taskbar behavior is not isolated.

comment.body: Thanks for providing the Dota 2 borderless-mode sequence and noting that reenabling Always On Top temporarily restores behavior. Could you confirm whether this still happens on the current PowerToys/Windows release, and whether it occurs with a different push-to-talk key as well? This will tell us whether the trigger is the game’s focus/z-order transition or a specific key path.
